To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Bitcoin's security guarantees apply to all PoW blockchains with the same consensus rules and parameters; (2) the PoW security of Bitcoin and its forks is independent from the underlying network topology and the number of participants; and (3) Bitcoin's security can be improved by adjusting its consensus and network parameters.
(1) the security of a PoW blockchain depends on the choice of the network and the consensus parameters and (2) the security of PoW blockchains is independent of the hash rate.

(1) the security of a PoW blockchain can be reduced to a single integer equation, (2) the solution of this integer equation can be found in polynomial time and (3) the security guarantees of Bitcoin and other PoW blockchains can be compared to the solution of the integer equation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
answering the following questions: 1) Is it possible for a malicious adversary to launch a successful attack against the Bitcoin blockchain?
the following questions: (i) What are the security guarantees of PoW blockchains instantiated with different parameters?
answering the following questions: (i) How do changes to the consensus parameters (e.g., the difficulty adjustment algorithm) affect the security of a PoW blockchain?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the security guarantees of Bitcoin are not transferable to forked PoWs.
the security guarantees of the Bitcoin blockchain apply to all other PoW blockchains, as they are based on the same security model and are subject to the same adversarial assumptions.

the security of a PoW blockchain is not only a function of the underlying parameters of the blockchain (e.g., the target block generation rate), but also depends on the specific parameters of the underlying consensus and network protocols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of a single miner, Bitcoin's security guarantees apply to any PoW blockchain with a single miner.

the security of PoW blockchains can be analysed using the same methodology as in Bitcoin, and that the security guarantees are not affected by the parameters of the PoW blockchain (e.g., block size, block time, etc.).
the security guarantees of Bitcoin and other PoW blockchains are similar in terms of the probability that a blockchain forks, but differ in the probability that the longest fork is invalid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although Bitcoin's security guarantees can be generalized, the security guarantees are not preserved for all parameter settings.
the security of Bitcoin's PoWs is not necessarily transferable to other variants.
the security guarantees of a PoW blockchain depend on the specific instantiation of the protocol, i.e., the consensus and the network parameters.
